accepted.question_text: For the space-homogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation in the regime gamma + 2s < 0, do global-in-time classical solutions exist? The paper identifies this very soft potential regime as unresolved even though homogeneous well posedness is understood when gamma + 2s >= 0.
accepted.context_brief: Homogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann, very soft potentials

evidence.quote: From a mathematical perspective, the homogeneous problem is significantly simpler than the inhomogeneous. The well posedness is well understood in the homogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation when γ + 2s ≥ 0. Remarkably, the existence of global in time classical solutions when γ + 2s < 0 remains open.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove a short-time existence theory for the inhomogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation with hard potentials and algebraically decaying initial data? The open case singled out in the paper is hard potentials gamma > 0 with initial data behaving like f_0 <= <v>^{-q}.
accepted.context_brief: Short-time existence with algebraic decay and hard potentials

evidence.quote: As far as we are aware, there are no further short-time existence results for the inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation without cutoff explicitly covered in the literature. The case of initial data with algebraic decay rate (as in f0 . hvi−q ), with hard potentials (γ > 0) is not handled by any documented result. It is remarkable that even though the Boltzmann equation is one of the most studied problems in mathematical physics, such a basic question still remains unanswered.

accepted.question_text: For the inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation with a physically meaningful collision kernel, do global classical solutions exist for generic initial data? This is the unconditional global well posedness problem outside perturbative or near-equilibrium regimes.
accepted.context_brief: Global classical well posedness for generic inhomogeneous data

evidence.quote: For any inhomogeneous model like (2.1), with a nontrivial and physically meaningful collision kernel Q, the global existence of classical solutions for generic initial data f0 remains an outstanding open problem.

accepted.question_text: In the space-homogeneous Boltzmann or Landau equation with gamma + 2s < 0, can one obtain an a priori L-infinity bound for classical solutions? The paper presents this missing estimate as the key obstruction in the very soft potential case.
accepted.context_brief: A priori L-infinity bounds in the very soft potential case

evidence.quote: Regularity estimates for the space homogeneous problem face a strong limitation when γ + 2s < 0. This range is called the very soft potential case. The Landau equation corresponds to s = 1, thus very soft potentials are those with γ < −2. Note that the very soft potential range is excluded from Theorems 3.1 and 3.2.The problem is that, even in the space homogeneous scenario, we do not know how to obtain an a priori estimate for the solution in L∞ when γ + 2s < 0.

accepted.question_text: For every classical solution f : [0, T] x R^3 -> [0, infinity) of the space-homogeneous Landau-Coulomb equation with initial data f_0, is the pointwise bound f(t, v) <= sqrt(250 / (9 pi)) max_w f_0(w) valid for all (t, v) in [0, T] x R^3? If true, this would rule out finite-time blow-up through a universal L-infinity estimate.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.3. Let f : [0, T ]×R3 → [0, ∞) be a classical solution of (7.1), where Q is the Landau-Coulomb operator (7.2), and f (0, v) = f0 (v). Then, for all values of (t, v) ∈ [0, T ] × R3 , we have the inequality f (t, v) ≤ sqrt(250/(9π)) max f0 (v).
Conjecture 7.3, if true, rules out the finite time blow-up for solutions to (7.1) in the Landau-Coulomb case.

accepted.question_text: Suppose f : (-infinity, 0] x R^3 -> [0, infinity) is a smooth classical solution of the space-homogeneous Landau-Coulomb equation, satisfies 0 <= f(t, v) <= 1 everywhere, and for every time t there is a constant C_t with integral f(v) <v>^{-1} dv <= C_t. Must f be a stationary Maxwellian?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.5. Let f : (−∞, 0] × R3 → [0, ∞) be a smooth classical solution of (7.1), where Q is the Landau-Coulomb operator (7.2). We make the following assumptions. • For all (t, v) ∈ (−∞, 0] × R3 , we have 0 ≤ f (t, v) ≤ 1. • For every t ∈ (−∞, 0], there is some constant Ct so that f (v)hvi−1 dv ≤ Ct . Then f must be a stationary Maxwellian.
However, a positive resolution of Conjecture 7.5 seems to be very difficult with current techniques.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove the hydrodynamic bounds (3.1), (3.2), and (3.3) for solutions of the inhomogeneous Landau and Boltzmann equations without assuming them a priori? Establishing those unconditional regularity estimates would imply global smooth solutions for arbitrary initial data.

evidence.quote: Observing the conditional regularity results of Theorems 3.2 and 3.1, the obvious question is whether the hydrodynamic bounds (3.1), (3.2) and (3.3) can possibly be proved.

If we somehow established the bounds for the hydrodynamic quantities in (3.1), (3.2) and (3.3), we would conclude that the inhomogeneous Landau and Boltzmann equations have global smooth solutions, for any initial data.

accepted.question_text: Can the Boltzmann equation, or the Landau equation, develop implosion-type singularities analogous to the singularities studied for compressible Euler or compressible Navier-Stokes? The paper presents this as a plausible alternative to unconditional regularity and notes that such singularities would invalidate the universal hydrodynamic bounds.

evidence.quote: There are some recent results studying the stability of implosion singularities for the compressible Euler equation, and producing singularities for the compressible Navier-Stokes equation (see [77] and [78]). Can there be similar implosion singularities for the Boltzmann equation? The idea is to look for a solution that mostly flows toward a single point.
If such an implosion singularity was indeed possible for the Boltzmann and/or Landau equation, then the bounds (3.1), (3.2) and (3.3) would not be true in general.

accepted.question_text: For a classical solution of the kinetic equation f_t + v · grad_x f = a_ij(t, x, v) partial_{v_i v_j} f on [0, 1] x B_1 x B_1 with uniformly elliptic coefficients lambda I <= {a_ij} <= Lambda I, does a Krylov-Safonov-type interior Holder estimate hold? In other words, must there exist alpha > 0 and C, depending only on dimension and ellipticity, such that ||f||_{C^alpha((1/2, 1) x B_{1/2} x B_{1/2})} <= C ||f||_{L^infinity([0, 1] x B_1 x B_1)}?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 8.1. Assume f : [0, 1] × B1 × B1 → R is a (classical) solution of an equation of the following form ft + v · ∇x f = aij (t, x, v)∂vi vj f.
Then, there exists constants α > 0 and C, depending only on dimension and the ellipticity parameters λ and Λ, so that kf kC α((1/2,1)×B1/2 ×B1/2 ) ≤ Ckf kL∞ ([0,1]×B1 ×B1 ) .

accepted.question_text: For a classical solution of the nonlocal kinetic equation (5.2) with bounded source term h and symmetric kernel K satisfying the two-sided fractional ellipticity bounds lambda |v' - v|^{-d-2s} <= K(t, x, v, v') <= Lambda |v' - v|^{-d-2s}, does a Krylov-Safonov-type interior Holder estimate hold? Specifically, can one prove the bound stated in Conjecture 8.2 with constants depending only on dimension, lambda, and Lambda?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 8.2. Assume f : [0, 1] × B1 × Rd → R is a (classical) solution of (5.2) for (t, x, v) ∈ (0, 1] × B1 × B1 and some bounded function h.
Then there are constants α > 0 and C, depending only on dimension, λ and Λ, so that f satisfies the estimate kf kC α ((1/2,1)×B1/2 ×B1/2 ) ≤ C kf kL∞ ([0,1]×B1 ×Rd ) + khkL∞ ([0,1]×B1 ×B1 ) .
As of now, both remain open.
